subject: Immediate action required — cloud region impact and traffic reroute instructions
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Li <sara.li@acme.com>, ops@betaretail.com
Cc: rachel.kim@redwood.ai, connor.obrien@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 13:12:00 +0000
Subject: Immediate action required — region impact and temporary routing options

Sara / BetaRetail team —

I wanted to reach you directly with a short, actionable plan. At 12:58 UTC we detected a provider-level networking degradation affecting our hosted control plane in parts of us-east and eu-west. This is impacting new session creation and token routing for some hosted customers in those regions. Our engineers have identified the problem and we are executing a cross-region failover, but there is a remaining window where some API calls may be routed unpredictably.

What you can do right now (pick one, easiest first):

1) Switch to region-specific hostname (recommended, immediate): point requests to a region-specific host to avoid control-plane routing. Examples:
   - US fallback: https://us.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
   - EU fallback: https://eu.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
   - APAC fallback: https://apac.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
   Note: These hostnames are identical in behavior to api.redwood.ai but bypass the affected regional routing path. No API key changes required.

2) Use the X-Redwood-Region header or query param as a temporary override (if changing hostnames is not feasible):
   - Header: X-Redwood-Region: us-west-2
   - Query: https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate?region=us-west-2
   This forces our edge to pin your session to the specified region for request processing.

3) If you run Dedicated capacity: we can route your tenant to a reserved pool in us-west-2 or eu-central-1. I am looping in Connor to confirm availability.

Operational notes and tradeoffs:
- Latency: routing to a non-local region may add 30–120ms depending on geo.
- Model behavior: no change in model outputs, but if you have token-budgeting or rate limits, you may want to use a lower-latency, higher-throughput variant (we suggest redwood-7b-quant for bursty workloads).
- DNS/TTL: if you change DNS records for api.redwood.ai, please use a low TTL (60s) during the window so we can revert quickly.

Attachments: rr-traffic-reroute-guide.pdf (step-by-step host/header examples), incident-timeline-20261120.csv (events), customer-notice-digest.txt

Next steps from us:
- We will publish an incident timeline and ETA on https://status.redwood.ai in the next 30 minutes.
- Connor will message availability for Dedicated reroute. Rachel will coordinate account-level communications and billing credit estimates if this impacts SLA.

Apologies for the disruption — we know this is time-sensitive. Please reply with which option you prefer and I will make the change on our side if you want us to.

— Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
[attachment: rr-traffic-reroute-guide.pdf (PDF)]

Thanks Stephanie — appreciate the quick note.

We can temporarily point to the us-specific host to avoid routing noise. Two quick asks before I change things on our side:
1) Can you confirm the exact CNAME and whether there is a path (e.g., /v1/generate) that we should not change?
2) Any risk of session tokens being invalidated when we switch hostnames mid-session?

If safe, we'll flip DNS and monitor in our staging first, then prod within the hour.

Sara

> 2) Any risk of session tokens being invalidated when we switch hostnames mid-session?

Sara — short answers below, and Connor / Rachel are cc'd for capacity and comms: 

1) Hostname/CNAME guidance:
   - Endpoint to use (no path changes): https://us.api.redwood.ai
   - If you are using a custom domain with a CNAME, point it to us.api.redwood.ai and keep the same path (/v1/generate, /v1/embeddings, etc.).
   - Example CNAME: api.acme-corp.com CNAME -> us.api.redwood.ai

2) Session tokens:
   - API keys remain valid. Session-level ephemeral token caches may be lost if a request is interrupted mid-stream; in practice, existing long-running streaming SSE connections will drop and need a reconnect. Short-lived, per-request tokens are not invalidated by hostname change.

Connor note: do you have capacity to accept two Dedicated tenants from the impacted pool if customers request fallback to reserved capacity?

Rachel: can you prepare a short bulletin for impacted customers with the recommended hostnames, expected latency delta, and suggested temporary model variant (redwood-7b-quant)? I attached the guide that has curl snippets and SDK examples.

— Stephanie

Hi all —

Quick update from infra: we have capacity in our us-west-2 and eu-central-1 reserved pools. If a dedicated fallback is required we can pin ACME and BetaRetail to those pools within ~20 minutes after signoff. Steps we will perform (owner: infra):

- Create tenant mapping to reserved pool (no API key rotation)
- Update routing rule with low TTL health checks
- Monitor token ingress and increase worker count if we observe CPU pressure

If you prefer the hostname switch only, that is fastest and has no service continuity risk other than short reconnects for streaming clients.

Status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2026-11-20-multi-region

I'll stay on this thread and coordinate the action.

— Connor
